reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to verify Alpha's refund work against the ledger, so I'll start by listing the refunds on record.
The ledger's refund list matches Alpha's handoff exactly, with the same two orders and amounts. Next I'll check the orders so I can confirm the refunds apply to real orders before paying anyone.

The ledger's refunds match Alpha's handoff, and both refunds are below their order amounts, so nothing looks wrong. Next I'll get the net balance for each customer, starting with acme, which has order 210 and refunded order 213.
Acme's net balance of 48125 matches the ledger: orders 210 (31647) and 213 (31611) minus refund 213 (15133). Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Birch's net balance of 67298 matches the ledger: orders 211 (38685) and 214 (35281) minus refund 214 (6668). Cobalt has no refunds, so I'll get its net balance next to finish the set.

Cobalt's net of 46961 matches its orders 212 (32516) and 215 (14445) with no refunds, and all three balances agree with the ledger. Alpha's refunds check out, so I'll record payouts, starting with acme's 48125.
Acme's payout is recorded. Birch's net balance of 67298 already matched the ledger, so I'll record that payout next.
Acme and birch are recorded, and cobalt's 46961 matched its orders with no refunds, so I'll record that last payout.
All three payouts were recorded successfully, and each matched its net balance from the ledger. Reporting the final payouts now.
